title: The agent reads the open workspace, so "this image" is the entry in front of the user
description:
UMBRELLA: MPI-889 - The agent works INSIDE the app, not beside it: it reads the workspace, moves the view, and hands a Flow over (consolidation sweep 2026-09-22). Members and phase order: tasks/MPI-889/plan.md.

PHASE 1, and the prerequisite for the other two. Fabio, 2026-09-22: 'If the user is in the history workspace, he shouldn't be forced to go into the gallery space to drag an image and send it to the agent. This means the agent needs to know which workspace it is working on ... the agent needs to look at the active entry, because the user has no way of sending something to the agent in that mode.' He is right that it cannot: `_appStateLine` (`agentLoop.mjs:747`) carries the open PROJECT and the image refs this conversation has touched, and nothing else. No page, no open card, no active entry. So with a card open and the user saying 'edit this image', the agent's only honest move today is `list_cards` or asking for an attachment - and in that workspace there is no drag surface to attach from. The channel already exists and the precedent is exact: `agentService.js:105` posts `{ project, mode, model, profileId, pinned }` every turn, and `pinned` IS renderer UI state shipped to the agent for exactly this kind of reasoning (what the settings panel is showing, so it can say that model makes video, not images). The workspace is one more key on that payload - roughly `workspace: { page, groupId, activeItemId }` - plus a clause in the App state line and one in the Cards rule (`agentLoop.mjs:1184`): with a card open, 'this image' is its active entry; do not call list_cards and do not ask them to attach anything. Watch the `_images` allowlist - the App state line is documented as the ONLY refs `look` and `generate` resolve, 'so the two cannot differ', so an entry named in the line has to be resolvable by the same path or the agent will name something it cannot then open.
